Urology Clinic Note

CC: Newly diagnosed prostate cancer, discuss active surveillance vs. definitive treatment

HPI: Mr. is a 62-year-old man with no significant comorbidities, referred after an elevated PSA of 6.1 ng/mL prompted a 12-core transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy. Pathology revealed adenocarcinoma of the prostate, Gleason 3+4 (Grade Group 2), involving 15% of one core with 6 mm of linear tumor length in FFPE tissue. Bone scan and pelvic CT obtained given intermediate-risk features show no evidence of metastatic disease. He has not received any pelvic radiation therapy or androgen deprivation therapy prior to this biopsy. He is otherwise healthy, runs 3 miles several times a week, and has an estimated life expectancy well over 10 years given his age and excellent overall health.

Assessment/Plan: Intermediate-risk, clinically localized prostate adenocarcinoma. Given the intermediate risk category and his desire to potentially avoid overtreatment, we discussed obtaining a genomic classifier assay on the FFPE biopsy tissue (which has adequate 6 mm linear tumor content) to help further risk-stratify and guide the choice between active surveillance and definitive treatment (radical prostatectomy vs. radiation therapy) in accordance with NCCN risk-stratification guidelines. He is an appropriate candidate for and is actively considering both active surveillance and definitive local therapy, and states he would change his decision based on the assay result. Genomic classifier testing was sent to the reference laboratory today. Result will be reviewed with the patient at follow-up to help finalize the treatment decision per current guideline-based algorithms.

Plan: 
- Send FFPE biopsy tissue for genomic classifier assay
- Return in 2-3 weeks to review results and finalize treatment decision
- Continue PSA monitoring in the interim
